quick: With or without food, same time each day
Start 1 mg; max 2 mg in moderate/severe CKD or HD
Contraindicated in acute liver failure / decompensated cirrhosis
Lipids, LFTs, CK if muscle symptoms, HbA1c/glucose
summary: Pitavastatin is an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor used as an adjunct to diet to lower LDL-C in adults with primary hyperlipidemia and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Dosed 2-4 mg once daily (max 4 mg), with reduced dosing in renal impairment. Contraindicated with cyclosporine and in active liver failure. Key risks are myopathy and rhabdomyolysis.
indications: Adjunct to diet to reduce LDL-C in adults with primary hyperlipidemia
Adjunct to diet to reduce LDL-C in adults with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH)

dosage.d: 2-4 mg once daily; maximum 4 mg once daily
dosage.t: Once daily, same time each day
dosage.n: If LDL-C goal not met or high-intensity statin needed at 4 mg, prescribe alternative LDL-lowering therapy

dosage.c: Moderate/severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-59) or ESRD on hemodialysis
dosage.d: Start 1 mg once daily; maximum 2 mg once daily
dosage.n: No adjustment needed for mild renal impairment

dosage.d: Do not exceed 1 mg once daily
Do not exceed 2 mg once daily
dosage.n: Rifampin markedly increases peak pitavastatin exposure

admin: Take orally once daily with or without food at the same time each day
Maintain a standard cholesterol-lowering diet throughout treatment
Assess LDL-C when clinically appropriate, as early as 4 weeks after initiation, and adjust dosage if needed
Do not exceed dosing caps when taken with erythromycin (1 mg) or rifampin (2 mg)
Reduce starting dose to 1 mg (max 2 mg) in moderate/severe renal impairment or hemodialysis
moa: Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme catalyzing conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate, the rate-limiting step in hepatic cholesterol synthesis. Reduced intracellular cholesterol upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, accelerating LDL uptake from blood and lowering plasma total cholesterol; sustained inhibition also decreases very-low-density lipoprotein levels.

absolute: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis
Hypersensitivity to pitavastatin or any excipient (angioedema, rash, pruritus, urticaria reported)
relative: Heavy alcohol use or history of liver disease
Predisposition to myopathy (age >=65, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, renal impairment)
monitor: Concomitant erythromycin, rifampin, fibrates, niacin >=1 g/day, or colchicine
Unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
Acute conditions predisposing to renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis

preg: Discontinue pitavastatin when pregnancy is recognized, or consider the ongoing therapeutic needs of the patient. Statins decrease cholesterol synthesis and may cause fetal harm based on mechanism of action; treatment of hyperlipidemia is generally not necessary during pregnancy. Observational data over decades have not identified a drug-associated risk of major congenital malformations.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. There is no information on the presence of pitavastatin in human milk, but another statin passes into human milk; because statins may cause serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, advise against breastfeeding.
renal: Renal impairment is a risk factor for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. For moderate and severe renal impairment (eGFR 30-59 and 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m2) and ESRD on hemodialysis, start 1 mg once daily with a maximum of 2 mg once daily. No adjustment for mild impairment. Monitor all renally impaired patients for myopathy.
hepatic: Contraindicated in patients with acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis. Increases in serum transaminases (some persistent) and rare fatal/non-fatal hepatic failure have occurred. Consider liver enzyme testing before initiation and as clinically indicated; discontinue if serious hepatic injury, hyperbilirubinemia or jaundice occurs.

major: Cyclosporine - increases pitavastatin exposure ~4.6-fold; concomitant use is contraindicated
Gemfibrozil - increased myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk; avoid concomitant use
Erythromycin - increases exposure ~2.8-fold; do not exceed pitavastatin 1 mg/day
Rifampin - increases peak exposure; do not exceed pitavastatin 2 mg/day
moderate: Fibrates (e.g., fenofibrate) - increased myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk; weigh benefit vs risk
Niacin lipid-modifying doses (>=1 g/day) - increased myopathy risk
Colchicine - reports of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis with statins
minor: Atazanavir - modest increase in pitavastatin exposure (~31% AUC)
Digoxin, diltiazem, enalapril, ezetimibe - no clinically significant interaction
interactions.food: High-fat meal decreases Cmax by 43% but does not significantly reduce AUC; grapefruit juice has minimal effect.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; substantial intake increases the risk of hepatic injury.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate creatine phosphokinase, transaminases, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and glucose/HbA1c.

serious: Increases in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose
rare: Cognitive impairment (memory loss, confusion; generally reversible)
emergency: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine)

monitoring: Lipid panel at baseline and as early as 4 weeks after initiation or dose change
Liver enzymes before initiation and when clinically indicated thereafter
Creatine kinase if unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness occurs
Renal function in patients at risk; monitor renally impaired patients for myopathy
counsel: Take once daily at the same time each day, with or without food
Promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness, especially with malaise or fever
Report fatigue, anorexia, right upper abdominal discomfort, dark urine or jaundice
Maintain a heart-healthy diet, regular exercise and healthy weight; glucose/HbA1c may rise
Inform provider of all medications, including OTC and herbal, and of known or suspected pregnancy
pk: LDL-C reduction within weeks of dosing
Store at 25 C (77 F), excursions 15-30 C; protect from light
pearls: Contraindicated with cyclosporine and not recommended with gemfibrozil due to myopathy risk
Metabolized mainly by glucuronidation (UGT) with only minimal CYP450 involvement
>99% protein bound; hemodialysis unlikely to be of benefit in overdose
Renal dose caps: start 1 mg, max 2 mg in moderate/severe CKD and hemodialysis
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose; do not double up. Resume the regular once-daily schedule.
overdose: No specific treatment for pitavastatin overdose is known. Provide supportive care and contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222). Hemodialysis is unlikely to be of benefit due to the high protein-binding ratio of pitavastatin.
